metadata.note: The Trinity and Brazos Valley Railway (the "Boll Weevil", advertised as the "Valley Road"), chartered Oct 1902: its own Cleburne - Hillsboro - Mexia line (1903-04), Mexia - Teague (1906), the Teague - Houston and Teague - Waxahachie main line (1907), and the trackage-rights legs its trains used into Dallas (Katy, 1907-1914), Fort Worth via Cleburne (Santa Fe, 1907-1908 confirmed) and Fort Worth via Waxahachie (H&TC, 1920-1930). Bought by the Colorado & Southern on 1 Aug 1905, which sold an undivided half to the Rock Island - a change of ownership, not of operator: the T&BV ran its own trains under its own name throughout, and its receivers (16 Jun 1914 - 1930) ran them as the T&BV. Renamed the Burlington-Rock Island Railroad on 7 Jul 1930 on leaving receivership; that is the one ownership split on this map, so every feature here ends by 1930 and the same trains continue in burlington_rock_island.geojson from 1930. Drawn from research/branches/trinity_and_brazos_valley_railway.txt (historical-trains repo, researched 2026-11-24), converted 2026-11-24. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS (last CONFIRMED year, not a known end): Cleburne - Mexia drawn 1904-1907 and Mexia - Teague drawn 1906-1907 - passenger service very probably ran later (Cleburne depot on the 1918 Sanborn map; Cleburne an operational endpoint after 1914; a Johnson County source says "1904 to 1924"), but no passenger year after 1907 is confirmed; abandonments were 1932 (Cleburne - Hillsboro), 1935 (Hillsboro - Hubbard), 1942 (Hubbard - Mexia), 1976 (Mexia - Teague), and Mexia - Teague was freight-only by 1951. Fort Worth - Cleburne over the Santa Fe drawn 1907-1908; the rights lasted to June 1914 but passenger use after 1908 is unconfirmed. SOURCE CONFLICTS recorded, not resolved: Fort Worth - Waxahachie over the H&TC from Oct 1915 (txrrhistory) vs 1920 (donsdepot) - drawn from 1920; donsdepot also dates the cancellation of trackage rights 1919 against 1914 (TSHA, txrrhistory); Cleburne - Mexia completion Nov 1903 (txrrhistory Tower 63) vs Jan 1904 (TSHA); charter date 7, 9 or 17 Oct 1902; Wikipedia's claim that the C&S leased the T&BV to the FW&DC in 1905 (no other source; treated as an error). Not established: whether 1908-1914 Fort Worth trains ran via Dallas over the Rock Island (a further trackage-rights leg, not drawn); the T&BV's pre-1911 Houston depot and its 1907-1914 Dallas (Cotton Belt) depot site; any T&BV frequency or running time - every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this layer is an estimate. Best next step: Chronicling America / Portal to Texas History for a "last train" item on each piece of the Cleburne - Mexia line, and a T&BV public timetable in any Official Guide 1908-1929.
metadata.branches_deliberately_omitted: Houston - Galveston (report block [8]): drawable NONE - the T&BV held trackage rights to Galveston (GH&N 1907-08, GC&SF from Apr 1908, GH&N/SP again from 1915), but no source shows T&BV PASSENGER trains on them; omitted until a timetable does. Also not drawn: any Fort Worth - Dallas leg over the Rock Island for 1908-1914 (unestablished).
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only is drawn. Mexia - Teague was freight-only by the Feb 1952 Official Guide (Table 58) and was abandoned in 1976; the Cleburne - Mexia pieces were abandoned 1932-1942. Those afterlives are mentioned in notes only; no segment runs past a confirmed passenger year.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Nothing to remove: the T&BV was steam-worked from its 1902-03 construction.
metadata.colour_choice: 2026-11-24: the T&BV is a new company on this map; #4B6B2A was chosen after checking programmatically that no feature in data/ uses it. It deliberately does NOT reuse #8E1B3C, the Colorado & Southern / Burlington-Rock Island family colour: the T&BV ran its own trains under its own name until 1930.

properties.line: Trinity and Brazos Valley: Houston – Waxahachie
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, not sourced (Rule 3): no T&BV public timetable or running time was found for any year (research report UNRESOLVED: "Frequencies and running times: none sourced for any T&BV year"). The figure is a typical early-1900s Texas branch-line steam speed, not a measurement.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, traced 2026-11-24 with opstrace.py (corridor Dijkstra over cached degree-tiles, Douglas-Peucker 8 m, reversals trimmed). Operator filter: OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=CB&Q;CRI&P (the joint Burlington / Rock Island tag OSM uses for the ex-T&BV / B-RI, on the live BNSF Houston and DFW Subdivisions) costed 1x; the Houston terminal approach traced separately over HB&T / UP terminal tracks.
properties.geometry_quality: 219.0 mi traced Houston (Union Station) - Tomball - Iola - Normangee - Teague - Corsicana - Waxahachie, against 218.0 mi documented (Fowler route 48, Waxahachie 0.0 to Houston 218.0) and 218.8 mi (Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 57, Waxahachie 30.8 to Houston 249.6 from Dallas). Traced mileposts from Waxahachie: Corsicana 30.5, Teague 66.0 (Fowler 66.6, Guide 66.8). No straight-line leg. 215.1 mi on OSM ways tagged CB&Q;CRI&P (BNSF Houston Subdivision Houston - Teague; BNSF DFW Subdivision Teague - Waxahachie), 2.5 mi untagged rail and 0.3 mi MP-tagged track at the Houston end, plus 1.2 mi over HB&T / Union Pacific terminal tracks from the North Houston end of the BNSF line to the Union Station throat (ends about 0.7 km east of the station building, whose own tracks are razed) and a 0.25 km joint between the two traces. LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEATS (Rule 2): the line is drawn on today's BNSF track, so any post-1930 line changes are not shown; the Houston end is drawn into Union Station for every year, but Union Station opened only in 1911 - for 1907-1910 the T&BV used another Houston depot (the report suggests the Cotton Belt depot, unverified), which is not drawn separately.

segments.note: The T&BV trunk. Teague - Houston opened with the first Fort Worth - Houston passenger train on 28 Jan 1907 (Houston Post of that day, "T&BV's first passenger train out of Houston", quoted by txrrhistory Tower 43; Tower 67 dates the Fort Worth - Houston service to the same day). Waxahachie - Teague (built north from Teague in 1907) carried the first Dallas - Houston through train on 1 Jul 1907 (Waxahachie Daily Light, 1 Jul 1907, via txrrhistory Tower 67). The receivership of 16 Jun 1914 - 1930 did not change the operator: the receivers ran the trains as the T&BV. Middle years rest on a Teague - Houston passenger run reported by the Teague Chronicle of 5 Jul 1911 (via Mike Cox), the Fort Worth - Waxahachie - Houston service of 1915/1920-1930, which ran over the whole of this line, system passenger revenue of $200,000 (1916) and $170,000 (1926) when this was the only through route, and unbroken continuation under the Burlington-Rock Island after 1930. Ends 1930 because the company was renamed the Burlington-Rock Island Railroad on 7 Jul 1930 on leaving receivership - a change of name, not an end of passenger service: the same trains continue on the B-RI feature bri-houston-fortworth-early (burlington_rock_island.geojson) from 1930. Headway 720 min (two trains each way a day) is an ESTIMATE, not sourced: no T&BV timetable frequency was found.
sources: Segment-level: start from the Houston Post of 28 Jan 1907 (txrrhistory Tower 43) and the Waxahachie Daily Light of 1 Jul 1907 (txrrhistory Tower 67); end at the 7 Jul 1930 renaming as the Burlington-Rock Island (TSHA B-RI entry; Fort Worth Press 8 Jul 1930 via txrrhistory Tower 63). The years 1912-1929 are NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL individually - no T&BV public timetable was found; they rest on the 1911 Teague Chronicle anchor, the 1915/1920 through service and the 1916/1926 passenger revenues. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Trinity and Brazos Valley: Dallas – Waxahachie (over the Katy)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, not sourced (Rule 3): no T&BV public timetable or running time was found for any year (research report UNRESOLVED: "Frequencies and running times: none sourced for any T&BV year"). The figure is a typical early-1900s Texas branch-line steam speed, not a measurement.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, traced 2026-11-24 with opstrace.py (corridor Dijkstra over cached degree-tiles, Douglas-Peucker 8 m, reversals trimmed). Operator filter: OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=MKT (the host railroad - this is Missouri, Kansas & Texas track) costed 1x; starts at the Waxahachie end of the T&BV main-line trace.
properties.geometry_quality: 30.1 mi traced Waxahachie - Red Oak - Lancaster - Dallas, against 30.8 mi documented (Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 57, Dallas to Waxahachie). No straight-line leg. 28.8 mi on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=MKT (today the BNSF DFW Subdivision north of Waxahachie - so the existing B-RI feature's Waxahachie - Dallas leg, traced on that subdivision, is indeed the ex-Katy alignment), 1.3 mi untagged rail at the Dallas end. The Dallas end stops at the south edge of downtown (about 1 km from the city centre): the T&BV's 1907-1914 Dallas station was the Cotton Belt depot (Fowler: "Dallas (SSW) ... 1911G", Cotton Belt depot "also used by Trinity & Brazos Valley"), whose site was not located, so the last mile into the depot is not drawn. LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEAT (Rule 2): drawn on the present-day track, not on a period map.

segments.note: TRACKAGE RIGHTS: this is Missouri, Kansas & Texas (Katy) track - the Katy's Dallas - Hillsboro line - over which T&BV trains ran between Dallas and the T&BV at Waxahachie. Dallas - Houston T&BV service began 1 Jul 1907 (Waxahachie Daily Light, 1 Jul 1907, via txrrhistory Tower 67). Fowler lists the T&BV at "Dallas (SSW)" in the 1911 Official Guide - the Cotton Belt depot, not Union Station (opened 1916). Ends 1914: the federal receivership judge cancelled all T&BV trackage rights in June 1914 (txrrhistory Tower 67; TSHA B-RI: Waxahachie - Dallas rights "canceled in 1914"), and "use of the Katy tracks to Dallas did not resume until the bankruptcy ended in 1930" - so there were NO T&BV trains into Dallas 1914-1930. 1912-1913 rest on continuity (S. G. Reed's "for several years"; the 1914 shared-signalling plan), not a timetable. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from the Waxahachie Daily Light of 1 Jul 1907 (txrrhistory Tower 67); 1911 from Fowler route 48 (1911 Official Guide listing at Dallas SSW); end at the June 1914 court cancellation of the Katy rights (txrrhistory Tower 67; TSHA B-RI entry). 1912-1913 and the headway are not sourced individually.

properties.line: Trinity and Brazos Valley: Cleburne – Mexia
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, not sourced (Rule 3): no T&BV public timetable or running time was found for any year (research report UNRESOLVED: "Frequencies and running times: none sourced for any T&BV year"). The figure is a typical early-1900s Texas branch-line steam speed, not a measurement.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, traced 2026-11-24 with opstrace.py (corridor Dijkstra over cached degree-tiles, Douglas-Peucker 8 m, reversals trimmed). Operator filter: OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=CB&Q;CRI&P (razed / abandoned grade) and OpenHistoricalMap ways named "Trinity and Brazos Valley Railway" (OHM ways 202454962 Cleburne - Hillsboro, 202447150 Hillsboro - Hubbard, 202455019 Hubbard - Mexia) costed 1x.
properties.geometry_quality: 77.8 mi traced Cleburne - Covington - Hillsboro - Malone - Hubbard - Coolidge - Mexia, against 78.0 mi documented (TSHA 78 mi; Fowler route 49, Cleburne 91.6 and Mexia 13.6 from Teague). No straight-line leg. 74.7 mi on ways of this railroad (OSM razed/abandoned ways tagged CB&Q;CRI&P and OHM T&BV ways - the whole line was lifted 1932-1942), 2.0 mi on the OHM Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe way into Cleburne (OHM ends the T&BV grade at its junction with the Santa Fe about 2 mi south of Cleburne station, so the last 2 mi into town are drawn on the Santa Fe alignment - the T&BV's own Cleburne approach and depot site are not mapped), 0.7 mi on an MKT-tagged way, 0.6 mi on an untagged OHM way. Waypoints all within 0.7 km of the line except Tehuacana (2.4 km - the station stood off the town).

segments.note: The T&BV's original railroad. Hillsboro - Mexia opened Oct 1903 and Hillsboro - Cleburne Jan 1904 (TSHA T&BV; txrrhistory Tower 43: extensions to Cleburne and Mexia "completed in early 1904"; Tower 63 says Nov 1903) - drawn from 1904, the later opening, so no year claims service on a piece not yet open. Fowler letters most stations "a" = the 1905 Official Guide, Mexia as the terminus of service in 1905. From 16 Mar 1906 it formed part of a Cleburne - Teague service, and from 28 Jan 1907 Fort Worth - Houston through trains ran over it; on 16 Dec 1907 the Railroad Commission ordered the T&BV to serve intermediate towns. [OPEN] END: passenger service confirmed to 1907. This is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end: no source dates when passenger service on this line actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Service almost certainly ran longer: the 1918 Sanborn map shows the T&BV Cleburne depot (it "closed as a railroad station in 1932") and Cleburne stayed an "operational endpoint" after June 1914, but neither proves passenger trains. A Johnson County source (unverified) says trains ran out of Cleburne "1904 to 1924". Abandonments - NOT passenger end years - were Cleburne - Hillsboro 1932, Hillsboro - Hubbard 1935, Hubbard - Mexia 1942; freight and the B-RI continued after the T&BV years. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from the TSHA T&BV entry (Oct 1903 / Jan 1904 openings) and txrrhistory Tower 43; 1905 from Fowler route 49 (1905 Official Guide); 1906-1907 from txrrhistory Tower 67 (16 Mar 1906 Cleburne - Teague trains; 28 Jan 1907 Fort Worth - Houston trains) and Tower 43 (RCT order of 16 Dec 1907). The 1907 end is the last confirmed year, not a sourced end. Headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: 13.9 mi traced Mexia - Limestone - Teague, against 13.6 mi documented (Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 58; Fowler route 49). No straight-line leg. 12.7 mi on razed OSM ways tagged CB&Q;CRI&P, 1.5 mi on an untagged OpenHistoricalMap railway way at Mexia.

segments.note: Built 1906 to meet the Mexia - Houston extension at Teague; "trains began operating between Cleburne and Teague on March 16, 1906" (txrrhistory Tower 67), and from 28 Jan 1907 the Fort Worth - Houston through trains ran this way. Crossed the H&TC at Tower 63 (Springfield). [OPEN] END: passenger service confirmed to 1907. This is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end: no source dates when passenger service on this line actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. The through trains were de-emphasised from c.1908 and no later passenger year is in hand for the T&BV era. By the Feb 1952 Official Guide (Table 58 "Mexia and Teague") the line was "Freight Service only", so passengers ended at an unknown year before 1951; the line was abandoned in 1976 - freight afterlife, not drawn. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from txrrhistory Tower 67 (16 Mar 1906 Cleburne - Teague trains); 1907 from the 28 Jan 1907 Fort Worth - Houston through service (Tower 67). The 1907 end is the last confirmed year, not a sourced end. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Trinity and Brazos Valley: Fort Worth – Cleburne (over the Santa Fe)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, not sourced (Rule 3): no T&BV public timetable or running time was found for any year (research report UNRESOLVED: "Frequencies and running times: none sourced for any T&BV year"). The figure is a typical early-1900s Texas branch-line steam speed, not a measurement.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, traced 2026-11-24 with opstrace.py (corridor Dijkstra over cached degree-tiles, Douglas-Peucker 8 m, reversals trimmed). Operator filter: OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=AT&SF (the host railroad - this is Gulf, Colorado & Santa Fe track, today the BNSF Fort Worth Subdivision) costed 1x; ends at the Cleburne end of the Cleburne - Mexia trace.
properties.geometry_quality: 28.2 mi traced Fort Worth (Santa Fe depot) - Crowley - Joshua - Cleburne, against about 28 mi (report figure, not sourced). No straight-line leg. 25.1 mi on OSM ways tagged AT&SF (BNSF Fort Worth Subdivision), 2.7 mi untagged rail in the Fort Worth terminal, and a 0.55 km joint to the T&BV junction at Cleburne. The report's "via Burleson" is not followed: Burleson is on the Katy (UP Fort Worth Subdivision, tagged MKT), not the Santa Fe; the Santa Fe main runs through Crowley, and an early trace through Burleson left the Santa Fe for the Katy. This feature duplicates the Santa Fe's own Fort Worth - Temple line (santa_fe_gulf_main_line.geojson) on purpose: it is a second company's trains on shared track. LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEAT (Rule 2): drawn on present-day BNSF track.

segments.note: TRACKAGE RIGHTS: this is Gulf, Colorado & Santa Fe track (the Santa Fe Fort Worth - Temple main line); the T&BV ran its Fort Worth - Houston trains over it from 28 Jan 1907 (Houston Post, via txrrhistory Tower 43; Tower 67), at first non-stop, until the Railroad Commission ordered on 16 Dec 1907 that they serve the intermediate towns. Drawn 1907-1908, the CONFIRMED span: by 11 Aug 1908 the Waxahachie Daily Light was reporting a planned move of Fort Worth traffic to a Rock Island - Katy - T&BV routing via Dallas, and txrrhistory says the T&BV "began to deemphasize operations on the Santa Fe route" within a year, so passenger use after 1908 is not confirmed. The bracket is 1907-1914: the rights themselves lasted until the receivership judge cancelled all T&BV trackage rights in June 1914. 1908 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - do not extend without evidence. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from the Houston Post of 28 Jan 1907 and the RCT order of 16 Dec 1907 (txrrhistory Tower 43); 1908 from the Waxahachie Daily Light of 11 Aug 1908 (Tower 43) and txrrhistory Tower 67; the June 1914 cancellation that bounds the bracket is from Tower 67 and the TSHA B-RI entry. Use after 1908 is not sourced. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Trinity and Brazos Valley: Fort Worth – Waxahachie (over the H&TC)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, not sourced (Rule 3): no T&BV public timetable or running time was found for any year (research report UNRESOLVED: "Frequencies and running times: none sourced for any T&BV year"). The figure is a typical early-1900s Texas branch-line steam speed, not a measurement.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, traced 2026-11-24 with opstrace.py (corridor Dijkstra over cached degree-tiles, Douglas-Peucker 8 m, reversals trimmed). Operator filter: OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=SP (the host railroad's successor - this is Houston & Texas Central track, built 1885-86 by the Fort Worth & New Orleans; today the UP Midlothian Subdivision) and OpenHistoricalMap ways named Texas & New Orleans / Fort Worth & New Orleans costed 1x; ends at the Waxahachie end of the T&BV main-line trace.
properties.geometry_quality: 41.4 mi traced Fort Worth - Mansfield - Midlothian - Waxahachie, against about 41 mi (report figure, not sourced). No straight-line leg. 41.0 mi on OSM ways tagged SP (UP Midlothian Subdivision), plus a 0.6 km joint at Waxahachie from the H&TC to the T&BV. The report's "via Venus" is NOT followed: neither the SP-tagged line nor OpenHistoricalMap's 1886 Texas & New Orleans ways pass Venus, which lies about 7 mi south on the Santa Fe (BNSF Venus Subdivision) and a razed MP-tagged line; an early trace forced through Venus produced a 9.5 mi straight line, so Venus was dropped. LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEAT (Rule 2): about 1.3 mi east of Mansfield (near 32.545 N, 97.05 W) the trace follows the post-1981 realignment of the UP line, not the 1886-1981 alignment that OHM maps about 110 m away (OHM way 205756196) - the T&BV-era alignment is the OHM one. Otherwise drawn on present-day UP track.

segments.note: TRACKAGE RIGHTS: this is Houston & Texas Central (Southern Pacific) track - the H&TC Fort Worth branch, built 1885-86 by the Fort Worth & New Orleans and leased to the H&TC. With the Santa Fe and Katy rights cancelled in June 1914, this was the receivership T&BV's only route into a big northern city: Fort Worth - Houston trains ran Fort Worth - Waxahachie over the H&TC and then over the T&BV main line. SOURCE CONFLICT on the start (recorded, not resolved): txrrhistory Tower 67 quotes the Waxahachie Daily Light of 11 Oct 1915 announcing T&BV Houston - Fort Worth service via Waxahachie "in six days" (about 17 Oct 1915), while donsdepot says the Fort Worth - Waxahachie trackage was "restored in 1920" over the H&TC. Drawn from 1920, the later of the two, because the 1915 evidence is an advance announcement, not a timetable; the bracket is 1915-1930 and 1915-1919 may well have run. Ends 1930: on the 7 Jul 1930 reorganisation the renamed Burlington-Rock Island resumed the Katy rights to Dallas and reached Fort Worth via Dallas, and the Fort Worth rights were "no longer considered necessary" (TSHA); the exact cut-over date was not found. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from donsdepot ("restored in 1920") - the later of the two conflicting dates; the earlier 1915 date is the Waxahachie Daily Light of 11 Oct 1915 via txrrhistory Tower 67. End from the 7 Jul 1930 reorganisation (TSHA B-RI entry). Years 1921-1929 and the headway are not sourced individually.
